passage: Nandini Amma was sorting chillies on her step in Kodur when the postmaster's grandson, Divyansh, home from the city, crouched to touch her feet. She saw him hesitate first, glancing at her face, as if unsure she would want it. Her knees ached and she disliked fuss, so she caught his hands halfway and held them. 'Enough, enough, son. Sit, tell me about your job.' Divyansh sat on the step, surprised, then smiling. Later, when the priest's young niece bowed to her at the temple, Nandini Amma let her, and laid a hand on the girl's head. Both times, she made sure to look them in the eye.

qa.q: What was Nandini Amma doing when Divyansh crouched?
How did Nandini Amma feel when she noticed Divyansh hesitate?
qa.a: She felt tender and a little protective towards him, sensing he was nervous and unsure whether she wanted the gesture.

qa.q: Which choice of Nandini Amma's made Divyansh feel seen, and why?
qa.a: Catching his hands and asking about his job, because it turned the bow into a real conversation instead of a test.

qa.q: How did Divyansh seem to feel when Nandini Amma stopped the bow?
qa.a: Divyansh looked surprised at first, then happy, as if relieved to be welcomed as a person rather than judged on the gesture.

grounding: Shows an elder who notices young people bend to touch her feet and either stops it warmly or blesses them, making sure each one feels seen rather than tested.

passage: After the Sunday service in Nyeri, Cucu Wanjiru watched young Paulo, home from his first job in Mombasa, come towards her and bend almost to one knee, the old way. Her own grandchildren just hugged her these days. She noticed his cheeks were flushed, as if he'd rehearsed it. She could have let him stay down. Instead she pulled him up by the shoulders. 'You don't need to bend for me, Paulo. Come, walk me home and tell me everything.' His shoulders dropped, and he offered her his arm. Behind them a little girl dropped a neat curtsy, and Cucu laid a hand on her head in blessing. Each got what they seemed to need.

qa.q: Where had Paulo just started working?
What did Cucu Wanjiru feel when she noticed Paulo's flushed cheeks?
qa.a: She felt fond and a little touched, sensing he had nervously rehearsed the old greeting to honour her.

qa.q: Why was lifting Paulo up and inviting him to walk a kind choice?
qa.a: It honoured his effort without making him perform, and turned the moment into real time together, so he felt seen rather than tested.

qa.q: How did Paulo seem to feel after Cucu Wanjiru pulled him up?
qa.a: Paulo seemed relieved and at ease; his shoulders dropped and he offered her his arm.

grounding: Illustrates an elder who sees a young person bend to greet her and gently declines, while blessing a child who curtsies, so that each feels seen rather than tested.
